item.title: Senior Associate Stakeholder Engagement Lead
item.description: We’re Ofwat, the Water Services Regulation Authority – a non-ministerial government department responsible for regulating the water sector in England and Wales. As the economic regulator of water and wastewater companies in England and Wales, our role is to enable, incentivise and hold companies to account for providing the very best for customers, communities and the environment. We also oversee the markets in the water sector to ensure they’re working for customers. Following the Independent Water Commission’s Final Report and subsequent White Paper - 'New Vision for Water', the UK government has set out a bold new direction - one that brings together expertise from across the sector to deliver better outcomes for customers and the environment. The Roles At this crucial time for the water sector, we are recruiting to three Stakeholder Engagement Lead roles to ensure we plan and deliver effective external engagement and communications to ensure the success of key strategic programmes. Each Stakeholder Engagement Lead role will be assigned to one of the following three priority areas for Ofwat: 1. Water efficiency campaign One of the available roles will be focused on our water efficiency campaign, Let's Save Water . Let's Save Water is a cross-regulatory behaviour change initiative co-owned by Ofwat, DEFRA, the Environment Agency, Natural England, the Drinking Water Inspectorate, Natural Resources Wales, and water companies. This is a high-profile campaign addressing one of England and Wales's most pressing environmental challenges, and you'll be at the heart of making it happen. 2. RAPID (Regulators' Alliance for Progressing Infrastructure Development) We're also looking for an experienced engagement professional to promote and explain the work of RAPID to a variety of stakeholders. RAPID is a partnership between Ofwat, the Environment Agency and the Drinking Water Inspectorate, established in 2019 to accelerate the development of major water supply infrastructure. Through the Major Water Infrastructure Programme, we are overseeing a pipeline of around 30 projects set out at Price Review 2024 and recently consulted on expanding RAPID's role to include the development of large-scale wastewater and other strategically important infrastructure projects. 3. Cross-cutting We also have one cross-cutting role, which will lead work within our central Stakeholder Engagement team across a range of priority programmes and activities. Key deliverables In this role you will be expected to: Develop, coordinate and deliver stakeholder engagement plans ensuring stakeholder views and insight are known and considered as part of key projects and programmes. Advise Ofwat's senior leaders on their engagement with key stakeholders, including in bilateral meetings, speaking engagements and visits. Work effectively and build strong relationships with key stakeholders and partners, ensuring high-quality standards of engagement are consistently delivered across projects and supporting effective and efficient coordination of our work plans. Deliver proactive external monitoring, capturing key insights and sharing these effectively to inform future engagement and internal decision-making. Oversee sentiment tracking and wider evaluation measures to ensure the successful delivery of engagement activity and continuous improvement of our approach. Work proactively with the wider Communications and Engagement team, sharing appropriate insights and working collaboratively across audiences and channels will support shared objectives. Manage and design speaking engagements, events and visits, working in partnership with stakeholders to design engaging and purposeful activities that build relationships, support effective communication of key messages, and support two-way engagement. Produce high-quality written and verbal communications to support stakeholder engagement, including briefing materials, key messages, speeches and presentations. About You Below are some of the key essential experience, skills & knowledge required for this post: 1. Lead criterion: Strong experience in designing and delivering strategic stakeholder engagement plans to support corporate priorities, including objective setting, strategy design and evaluation. 2. Experience in building and maintaining strong relationships with stakeholders, both internally and externally and including senior leaders. 3. Excellent verbal and written communication skills and attention to detail including the ability to write clearly and in a tailored way for a range of audiences. 4. The ability to work collaboratively with people across teams and levels, ensuring the effective involvement of a range of partners in the development and delivery of engagement plans. It is desirable but not essential to have experience working with external stakeholders, agencies or contractors to deliver campaigns, projects or events. Why You Should Join Us: People Centric: Our people are at the heart of Ofwat and everything we do - we ensure all voices are heard and treat each other with respect; you'll be given the autonomy and the support to do your role in the best way. Innovative Work Environment: We embrace agile and new ways of working and have a culture build on trust, flexibility, and collaboration. Development Opportunities: Gain valuable experience and develop your skills in a supportive and dynamic setting. Work-Life Balance: Enjoy the flexibility of working from home combined with the benefits of in person collaboration in our Birmingham offices. Good employer pension contributions 25 days’ annual leave, increasing to 30 with each year of service, plus bank holidays and an extra 2.5 days of privilege leave. Access to exclusive discounts on a variety of goods and services, including retail outlets, theatre tickets, holidays, insurance, and a gym membership. Fees paid for membership of relevant professional bodies. Up to 3 volunteering days per year. Recognition vouchers scheme rewarding your hard work. Generous shared parental leave and pay supporting your family life. To Apply Please click on the Apply button below for more information and to download the Candidate Pack, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:55pm on Sunday 11th October 2026

item.title: Press Officer Associate
item.description: Join Ofwat’s Communications and Engagement team as a Press Officer Associate in the Press Office team. About Us We’re Ofwat, the Water Services Regulation Authority – a non-ministerial government department responsible for regulating the water sector in England and Wales. As the economic regulator of water and wastewater companies in England and Wales, our role is to enable, incentivise and hold companies to account for providing the very best for customers, communities and the environment. We also oversee the markets in the water sector to ensure they’re working for customers. Following the Independent Water Commission’s Final Report and subsequent White Paper - 'New Vision for Water', the UK government has set out a bold new direction - one that brings together expertise from across the sector to deliver better outcomes for customers and the environment. The Role The Press Office is the guardian of Ofwat’s reputation. We work to both protect of the reputation of the organisation and promotion of its work proactively. We work with organisations across the modern media landscape – national and local newspapers, broadcast, trade and specialist media, and online, digital media outlets. The Press Office manages the media handling on behalf of the organisation. We work closely with colleagues in other communications teams to deliver on our strategy, including the public affairs, digital, stakeholder and marketing teams. At a crucial time for the water sector, you will contribute to, and help deliver, our media strategy, building on our overall communications strategy and ensuring that we target media stakeholders effectively, deliver the right messages across to the right audiences, and strengthen our horizon scanning. Key deliverables In this role you will be expected to: Work within the press team and its functions, servicing media questions, bids and briefing from journalists across the media landscape to enhance and protect the reputation of the organisation. Work closely with colleagues, including policy officials and senior leadership, to advise on the role communications can play and media handling approaches. Work on proactive media handling, including drafting press releases and developing proactive media tactics that will get cut through in a competitive media landscape. You will work with policy teams to agree messaging and maximise media opportunities. Advise and ensure that senior leaders are supported by press office, including briefing on relevant news stories and emerging issues as required. Build relationships with journalists across print, broadcast and trade and consumer, digital media. Complete analysis and evaluation tasks to gather insight and promote best practice within the team and beyond. Take part in out of hours media duty, including occasion work at weekends and on bank holidays. Work with partner regulators and central government on water-related issues. Carry out additional duties and support projects appropriate for the role. About You Below are some of the key essential experience, skills & knowledge required for this post: 1. Lead Criteria: Strong oral and written communication skills, including the ability to write clearly and concisely. 2. Lead Criteria: Interest, knowledge and awareness of the modern media landscape. 3. Experience working with media and the press, including new media outlets. 4. Ability to influence and network with stakeholders internally and externally, including senior management and journalists. 5. Ability to horizon scan and spot upcoming risks and opportunities. 6. Administration and digital skills, and excellent attention to detail. Why You Should Join Us: People Centric: Our people are at the heart of Ofwat and everything we do - we ensure all voices are heard and treat each other with respect; you'll be given the autonomy and the support to do your role in the best way. Innovative Work Environment: We embrace agile and new ways of working and have a culture build on trust, flexibility, and collaboration. Development Opportunities: Gain valuable experience and develop your skills in a supportive and dynamic setting. Work-Life Balance: Enjoy the flexibility of working from home combined with the benefits of in person collaboration in our Birmingham offices. Good employer pension contributions 25 days’ annual leave, increasing to 30 with each year of service, plus bank holidays and an extra 2.5 days of privilege leave. Access to exclusive discounts on a variety of goods and services, including retail outlets, theatre tickets, holidays, insurance, and a gym membership. Fees paid for membership of relevant professional bodies. Up to three volunteering days per year. Recognition vouchers scheme rewarding your hard work. Generous shared parental leave and pay supporting your family life. We have 1 Fixed Term contract available until the end of December 2027. *Office Location: London (E14 4HD) or Birmingham (B5 4UA) with hybrid working* To Apply Please click on the Apply button below for more information and to download the Candidate Pack, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:55pm on Sunday 11th October 2026

item.description: Join the PubAffairs Network Established in January 2002, PubAffairs is the premier network and leading resource for the public affairs, government relations, policy and communications industry. The PubAffairs network numbers over 4,000 members and is free to join. PubAffairs operates a general e-Newsletter, as well as a number of other specific group e-Newsletters which are also available to join by completing our registration form. The PubAffairs e-Newsletters are used to keep members informed about upcoming PubAffairs events and networking opportunities, job vacancies, public affairs news, training courses, stakeholder events, publications, discount offers and other pieces of useful information related to the public affairs and communications industry. item.title: Account Director (Health | Life Sciences | Public Affairs)
item.description: PLMR Healthcomms a leading UK healthcare public affairs and communications consultancy. We help organisations get health innovation moving. Working across pharmaceuticals, medical technology, diagnostics, digital health and the wider NHS, we help clients navigate complex policy and NHS structures to turn innovation into real-world impact. As the NHS continues to evolve, organisations need advisers who understand how decisions are made across government, Parliament and the NHS. Our team combines expertise in health policy, public affairs, strategic communications and stakeholder engagement to help clients shape policy, build trust and accelerate adoption. As part of the wider PLMR Group, we bring together specialists in communications, digital, political intelligence and AI-enabled insight to deliver integrated campaigns that influence policy, change perceptions and create measurable impact. We judge our success by the difference we make for our clients - whether that's influencing policy, strengthening partnerships, changing conversations or helping innovative products and services reach patients more quickly. Key Responsibilities and Duties We're looking for an experienced and ambitious Account Director to help lead the next stage of PLMR Healthcomms' growth. This is an opportunity to work at the heart of some of the most important challenges facing healthcare today. You will be supporting organisations to navigate NHS reform, shape policy, build stakeholder confidence and ultimately improve patient access to medicines, technologies and services. You will act as a trusted adviser to clients across pharmaceuticals, medical technology, diagnostics and digital health, helping them move from ambition to action. Alongside leading strategic client programmes, you will play an important role in developing our growing healthcare practice, supporting new business, mentoring colleagues and helping strengthen PLMR Healthcomms' reputation as the consultancy that gets health innovation moving. The ideal candidate will bring: A passion for improving healthcare through policy, communications and stakeholder engagement. Significant experience advising pharmaceutical, life sciences or health technology organisations, ideally with agency experience. An excellent understanding of the NHS, Government, Parliament and the wider healthcare policy landscape. Confidence advising senior clients through complex policy, political and reputational challenges. A commercial mindset and enthusiasm for helping grow both clients and the wider business. A collaborative approach and a desire to develop colleagues while contributing to a supportive, ambitious team. Key Skills and Competencies Significant experience in healthcare public affairs, integrated communications or healthcare consultancy. A strong understanding of the political and NHS landscape and how healthcare decisions are made. Experience advising pharmaceutical, medtech or life sciences organisations. A track record of leading strategic client relationships and delivering measurable outcomes. Excellent commercial awareness and experience contributing to business growth. Outstanding communication, leadership and mentoring skills. Curiosity, ambition and a desire to help shape the future of healthcare. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more about this role. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Saturday 31st October 2026

item.title: Research Manager(s)
item.description: More in Common is seeking at least one, possibly two, Research Managers to oversee and deliver high-quality research projects. They will work across our core areas of research for clients, media and communications, political polling and partnerships; More in Common UK is a small team with a start-up culture where everyone is expected to execute a range of responsibilities. The role will be based in our London office Monday-Thursday with Friday at the office or working at home. ABOUT MORE IN COMMON More in Common is a research agency working across the US, UK, Germany, France, Spain and Poland to tackle polarisation and division. More in Common leads and supports initiatives to build more united, inclusive, and resilient societies. Our mission is to understand the forces driving us apart, help societies find common ground and bring people together to tackle shared challenges. In the UK, our work is best described as being part consultancy and part think tank. We provide a full suite of research services including polling and focus group research; evidence reviews and secondary data analysis; audience mapping and audience strategy; strategic communications strategy and campaign development. More in Common are members of the British Polling Council. ABOUT THIS ROLE We are open to the role having more of a quantitative or qualitative specialism, depending on candidates’ previous experiences (such as in polling, think tanks, research or consultancy). People who thrive at More in Common tend to have the following qualities: exceptional intelligence, the drive and passion to go the extra mile, a strong sense of high standards and pride in their work, the ability to tell a story or make an argument (whether that’s on paper or out loud), a great sense of humour, and the aptitude and desire to work in a fast-paced environment, juggling multiple priorities at once. Research Design and manage quantitative and qualitative research projects from inception to delivery, ensuring methodological rigour Provide excellent client management to our partners and ensure all outputs for clients are high-quality Lead on survey design, questionnaire development, and analysis of public opinion data, including complex polling and focus group datasets and transcripts Synthesise findings into clear, compelling narratives that provide actionable insights for clients Stay abreast of developments in research methodology, polling practice, and the UK public opinion landscape, bringing new approaches into More in Common's work Contribute to the development of More in Common's research agenda, identifying gaps and opportunities for new projects Secure new research projects for More in Common by building relationships with and reaching out proactively to potential partners, cultivating opportunities in areas of relevance to our mission External Engagement Represent More in Common in external settings including media appearances, roundtables, events and conferences Communicate research findings to diverse audiences including policymakers, civil society, and the media Build and maintain relationships with research partners, academic institutions, and partner organisations Management Line-manage and support the development of research associates, providing day-to-day guidance, feedback, and structured professional development Contribute to organisational planning and team management processes Support a hard-working, intellectually-curious and fun team culture, modelling More in Common's values internally and externally Play an active role in organisational development, including contributing to hiring processes, onboarding QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE We look for great people before we look for specific qualifications and experience - so we are always open to applications from candidates with great potential but limited experience. However, for this role we are looking for someone with experience leading research projects for clients in a professional, rather than academic, setting: for example, in a think tank, polling company, research agency, comms or PR firm or other policy, public opinion or political organisation. The role is less suitable for someone whose primary experience is academia as we are looking for applied professional experience leading projects. To Apply Please click on the Apply button below for more information, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Indicative Timeline (please note these dates remain subject to change): Initial conversation with a hiring manager: 5 – 16 October Interviews – w/c 19 October We expect to make an offer to the successful candidate by late October. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Sunday 4th October 2026

item.title: Public Affairs Officer
item.description: Groundwork UK is looking for a Public Affairs Officer to help put its new three-year public affairs strategy into action. About Us Groundwork UK is the national body of the Groundwork federation, supporting, championing and representing the work of Groundwork Trusts across the country. This includes building national relationships with funders and policymakers, securing resources to support local delivery and acting as a managing agent for programmes and contracts delivered by Groundwork Trusts and other partners. Groundwork takes practical action to create a fair and green future in which people, places, and nature thrive. We support local communities and businesses to build capacity and resilience as this is vital if we are to tackle hardship, achieve a just transition to net-zero and help nature recover in a way that reduces inequality and leads to better work and healthier, happier lives. About the Role This is a hands-on role focused on strengthening Groundwork’s political visibility, building relationships with key stakeholders, and supporting the federation to make a clear and compelling case for place-based environmental and social action. Working with the Head of Policy & Communications, the postholder will map and engage national, regional and devolved political stakeholders; maintain intelligence on policy developments and opportunities; and help Groundwork Trusts prepare for and follow up political engagement. The role will also support the development of briefings, correspondence, stakeholder materials and core messages that explain Groundwork’s role and impact. About You We are looking for someone with a genuine enthusiasm for politics, strong written communication skills and the judgement to understand what matters, what will land and how relationships are built over time. You will be organised, self-motivated and comfortable working with senior colleagues and external stakeholders across government, combined authorities, civil society and the wider policy landscape. To Apply If you would like to find out more, please click the Apply button below. You will be directed to our website where you will be able to download the Job Description and Recruitment Pack, and to complete your application for this position. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Interview Details: Week commencing 16 November - Birmingham office. We value diversity and flexibility in our workforce as we think it gives us access to a wider range of skills. We therefore strive to be an equal opportunities employer. Where appropriate, we ask our workers to complete a Disclosure and Barring Service (Criminal Records Bureau) check. No agencies please. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Friday 30th October 2026
